exposure: patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) vs. nurse-administered opioid analgesia (non-PCA)
outcome: opioid consumption (average daily oral morphine milliequivalents)
cohort: The study included 224 patients aged 18 years or older who were initiated on analgesia within 24 hours of surgery.
finding: Patients receiving PCA demonstrated significantly increased opioid consumption, longer hospital stays, and a higher incidence of nausea compared to those receiving nurse-administered opioid analgesia.
